<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|410|THE EPISTLE OF S. PAVL|CHA. XI.}}</noinclude>ansvver vnto him? ''I haue left me seuen {{sup|‖}} thousand men, that haue not bovved their knees to '' {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Heretics adde here also, ''Image,'' to the text, as ''Act. 19, 35.''}}∷ ''Baal''? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=5}}† So therfore at this time also, there are remaines saued according to the election of grace.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=6}}† And if by grace: {{sup|‖}} not novv of vvorkes. othervvise grace now is not grace. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=7}}† Vvhat then? that vvhich Israel sought, the same he hath not obtained: but the election hath obtained: and the rest vvere blinded. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=8}}† as it is vvritten: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 6, 9.''}}* ''{{sup|‖}} God hath giuen them the spirit of compunction: eies, that they may not see: and eares, that they may not heare: vntil this present day''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}}† And Dauid saith: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 68, 23.''}}* ''Be their table made for a snare and for a trappe and for a scandal and for a retribution vnto them''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}}† ''Be their eies darkened, that they may not see: and their backe make thou alvvaies crooked''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}}† I say then, haue they so stombled, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Iewes are not reiected wholly & incurably for euer: but for a part, and for a time suffered to fall. Which God did turne to the Gentils general good.}}∷ that they should fall? God forbid. but by their offence, saluation is to the Gentils, that they may emulate them. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† And if the offence of them be the riches of the vvorld, and the diminution of them {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ If God could and did turne their fall and sinne into the good of the Gentils, much more wil he worke good of their general conuersion, which shalbe at length the accomplishment of the Church consisting of both the Nations.}}∷ the riches of the Gentils: hovv much more the fulnesse of them? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† For to you Gentils I say, as long verely as I am the Apostle of the Gentils, I vvil honour my ministerie, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† if by any meanes I may prouoke my flesh to emulation, and may saue some of them. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† For if the losse of them be the reconciliation of the vvorld: vvhat shal the receiuing be, but life from the dead? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† And if the first fruite be holy, the masse also: and if the roote be holy, the boughes also. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† And if some of the boughes be broken, and thou vvhereas thou vvast a vvilde oliue, art graffed in them, and art made partaker of the roote and of the fatnesse of the oliue, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† glorie not against the boughes. And if thou glorie: not thou bearest the roote, but the roote thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† Thou saiest then: The boughes vvere broken, that I might be graffed in. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† Vvel: {{sup|‖}} because of incredulitie they vvere broken, but thou by faith doest stand: be not to highly vvise, but {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We see that he which standeth by faith, may fall from it, and therfore must liue in feare, and not in the vaine presumption and securitie of the Heretikes.}}∷ feare. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21}}† For if God hath not spared the natural boughes: lest perhaps he vvil not spare thee neither. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22}}† See then the goodnes and the seueritie of God: vpon them surely that are fallen, the seueritie: but vpon thee the goodnes of God, if thou abide in his goodnesse, othervvise thou also shalt be cut of. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=23}}† But they also, if they do not abide in incredulitie, shal be graffed in. for God is able to graffe them in againe. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=24}}† For if thou vvast cut out of the natural vvild oliue, and contrarie to nature vvast graffed into the good oliue: hovv much more they that are according to<noinclude>{{rh|||nature,}}</noinclude>
